$description: Cover images: the working paper. Every cover is one piece of evidence taped into an audit file and ticked by the auditor. scripts/cover-prompt.mjs turns this file into the prompt for an image model. {tape} and {redline} resolve from tokens/tokens.json.
brief: Fine-art editorial cover illustration for an accountancy publication, built like an auditor's working paper. Follow this system precisely.

layers.ground: A pure black page with very faint ledger ruling in dark charcoal: thin horizontal rules, two or three vertical column rules, and one double rule near the bottom, like the ghost of a ledger sheet. No numbers on it.
layers.evidence: Exactly one real object, photographed in hard raking museum light, printed as a cut-out black-and-white photo in coarse halftone (visible round dot screen, film grain, photocopy toner noise, crushed blacks). The cut-out has a clean scissor-cut edge (never torn) and sits on the page rotated two or three degrees.
layers.fixing: Exactly ONE short strip of flat calculator-tape yellow {tape} masking tape across one top corner of the cut-out, as if taped into an audit file.
layers.mark: Exactly ONE small hand-drawn red-pencil mark in {redline}, either a single audit tick beside the key detail or a single loose circle around it, never both. It looks hand-drawn and slightly imperfect, never digital.

rules: Yellow and red are the only colours; everything else is black-and-white halftone.
One clear focal point slightly off-centre, at least 50 percent empty space, the evidence no larger than half the frame, calm and expensive, like the cover of a serious design magazine.
Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, labels or logos anywhere.

tax.object: an old steel receipt spike on a small round base, holding a neat stack of paper receipts with no readable text
alternatives: a rubber date stamp on its pad
a stack of sealed window envelopes

audit.object: a vintage brass-rimmed magnifying loupe resting on a ruled ledger page with blank rows
audit.where: beside one row seen through the lens
alternatives: a filing drawer pulled half open
a bulldog clip holding a thin sheaf of papers

finance.object: a 1950s ten-key desktop adding machine with a crank handle on the side and a short curl of paper tape coming out of the top, seen from a low three-quarter angle; clearly an adding machine with a small square keypad, not a typewriter
alternatives: a steel cash box with its lid open

data.object: a short cascade of continuous fan-fold computer printout paper with faint alternating grey bands and sprocket holes, falling in neat folds
alternatives: a fanned stack of punched cards

ai.object: the elegant hand of an 18th-century brass clockwork automaton, refined and delicate rather than robotic, holding a quill pen
alternatives: the exposed brass gear train of an automaton's wrist
a clockwork bird perched on a ledger

practice.object: a weathered Hellenistic marble bust of a thoughtful man in three-quarter view, cut out at the shoulders
alternatives: a marble hand resting on a closed ledger
a marble hand offering a plain card

podcast.object: a 1940s ribbon broadcast microphone on a short chrome desk stand, its cable trailing off
alternatives: a pair of studio headphones resting on a closed ledger

checks: One fixing and one mark. Two strips of tape, or a tick and a circle together, means regenerate.
Count the hands. Poses with two hands often come out with a third.
No legible text or numbers. Realistic keypads tend to show digits; look closely.
The object says the topic without a caption.
